title: Route Execution Inspector: compact traces, sharded index, and policy-effectiveness metrics
creator: Aisha Patel
description:
Goal: Ship a lightweight Route Execution Inspector that captures an explainable, queryable snapshot of a routing decision for each sampled request, enables low-latency searches across high-cardinality routing attributes, and surfaces a policy-effectiveness metric to help PM/TPs evaluate fallbacks and regional routing efficiency.

Background: Current routing observability streams are high-fidelity but expensive and difficult to query for ad-hoc investigations. Existing artifacts provide per-hop telemetry and provenance events, but we need: (1) a compact per-request trace that retains enough context to explain why a request took a route, (2) an index sharding strategy to support sub-second queries over tens of millions of traces per day, and (3) a small set of derived metrics (policy-effectiveness score, fallback frequency, warmed-cache ratio) to drive dashboards and regression alerts.

Scope: Implement the inspector end-to-end for hosted API traffic (first tenant), with sampling controls, storage in a sharded decision-index (time + model-variant shards), UI endpoint for quick-inspect (Console quick-inspect modal), and backend pipelines to compute policy-effectiveness and per-step timings. Private/Dedicated rollout is out of scope for this ticket but the schema will be compatible.

Non-goals: Do not ship full request payloads or raw model outputs. This inspector only stores routing metadata and short context hashes. Full tracing of model tokens will be provided by separate tracing pipelines.

Success metrics:
- Median time to fetch a sampled trace in Console quick-inspect < 350ms for recent shards.
- Policy-effectiveness alert precision > 90% when validated against manual review of 200 incidents.
- Storage cost for inspector traces < 3% of current full-provenance stream cost for equivalent sample rate.

Design summary:
1) Compact trace format: protobuf v2 with a reduced schema (route steps, decisions, latency buckets, cache-warm flag, fallback fingerprint, region & tier tags) compressed with zlib and stored as base64 to preserve JSON pipelines. Max uncompressed fields limited to 1KB.
2) Sampling: adaptive stratified sampler that ensures representation across model variants, regions, and error classes. Default sample rate 1% with adjustable overrides per project and emergency 100% mode for incident window.
3) Sharded decision index: primary shards by YYYYMMDD + model-variant hash (8-bit) to keep hot-day queries localized; retention TTL 30d for full traces, 90d for derived metrics. Index supports queries by request_id, customer_id, decision_hash, and fallback_tag.
4) Derived metrics worker: stream jobs compute policy-effectiveness = weighted success of first-choice route given latency & error SLOs, fallback frequency per 100k requests, and cache-warm ratio. Metrics emitted to Prometheus and to Console timeseries dashboards.
5) Console UI: quick-inspect modal shows timeline, first-choice rationale, fallback reason, and links to the raw provenance snapshot when available.

Trade-offs considered:
- Storage vs fidelity: we limit trace size and store hashes to avoid storing full contexts. This reduces ability to replay exact prompts but keeps cost low.
- Query latency vs write amplification: sharding by day+variant reduces cross-shard reads but requires careful rollover handling.
- Privacy: traces avoid PII; security review required for KMS usage on indexing metadata.

Rollout plan: feature-flagged rollout to internal traffic (2 days), then 5 pilot customers (2 weeks), then GA on hosted with toggles for sample rate per-customer. Dedicated/Private follow-ups to add on-prem storage connectors.
acceptance_criteria: Compact trace schema documented in Confluence + JSON schema file checked into repo
End-to-end write path: sampled request produces inspector trace and it is queryable via index within 60s
Console quick-inspect modal can fetch and render a sampled trace with timeline and fallback reason
Derived metrics worker emits policy-effectiveness and fallback-frequency metrics to Prometheus and Console dashboard
Adaptive sampler respects per-customer overrides and emergency 100% mode
implementation_notes: Backend: add route-inspector producer in routing-service that emits to inspector-kafka topic (compact, zlib-compressed protobuf)
Storage: decision-indexer consumes inspector topic, writes compressed blobs to s3-friendly buckets partitioned by YYYY/MM/DD/variantHash
Indexing: lambda job builds Glue/ElasticSearch shards for fast query; consider ClickHouse for low-latency point lookups
Metrics: worker computes per-request signals and aggregates into Prometheus histograms and a timeseries table for Console
Sampling: implement adaptive stratified sampler in routing-service with lightweight counters and periodic recalibration job
